properties.title: NRC Report: Benzene near Mont Belvieu, TX
properties.summary: Incident Type: FIXED - NRC Report ID: 889349 - Medium Affected: AIR - Suspected Responsible Party: CONOCOPHILLIPS
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 889349
Incident Time: 2008-11-06 01:00:00
Nearest City: Mont Belvieu, TX
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: BENZENE
Medium Affected: AIR
Suspected Responsible Party: CONOCOPHILLIPS
Skytruth Analysis
GULF COAST FRACTIONATORS AND ITS NEIGHBORING PLANT ONEOK SHARE THE SAME OIL CIRCUIT BREAKER AT THE ELECTRIC SUBSTATION. WHEN ONEOK WAS PERFORMING REPAIR WORK ON THEIR TRANSFORMER, THE SUDDEN PRESSURE SWITCH VALVE TRIPPED (IT WAS BLOCKED IN AND THUS SHOULD NOT HAVE TRIPPED) AS THE VALVE HAD A LEAK. SINCE BOTH THE PLANTS SHARE THE SAME OCB, PROBLEMS WITH ONEOK'S TRANSFORMER TRIPPED THE OCB AND THE MAIN BREAKERS TO BOTH THE PLANTS THUS CAUSING GULF COAST FRACTIONATORS TO LOOSE POWER ON NOV 5, 2008. DURING PLANT STARTUP, PROBLEMS WITH THE BLOWER MOTOR IN THE INCINERATOR CAUSED IT TO SHUTDOWN AT 20:00 PM ON NOV 5, 2008. THE BLOWER MOTOR WAS REPLACED AND THE INCINERATOR WAS RETURNED TO NORMAL OPERATING CONDITIONS AS OF 13:00 PM ON NOV 6, 2008. THE BENZENE EMISSIONS WERE CAUSED DUE TO THE VAPORS EMANATING FROM THE GASOLINE STORAGE TANKS. THE SAME INCIDENT WAS REPORTED TO NRC ON NOV 5, 2008 (NRC INCIDENT NO. 889279). HOWEVER, THIS ADDITIONAL REPORT IS BEING SUBMITTED AS WE HAVE THE FINAL EMISSION NUMBERS FOR BENZENE.

properties.content:
Report Details

Nearest City: Newark, NJ
Location: OAK ISLAND RAILYARD
Incident Type: RAILROAD
Material: OIL: DIESEL
Medium Affected: RAIL REPORT (N/A)
Suspected Responsible Party: CONRAIL CONSOLIDATED
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 40.709824, -74.143226 (Approximated from establishment)
Reported Spill Volume: 450 gallon
Report Description///THIS IS AN UPDATE TO NRC REPORT 1435771/// UPDATED INFO IS AS FOLLOWS: THE RELEASE WAS FROM AN ENGINE. THE ENGINE STRUCK A BOLT THAT WAS STICKING OUT OF A RETARDER, DUE TO EQUIPMENT FAILURE, WHICH CAUSED THE RELEASE. ENGINE NUMBER IS CSX4406. ENGINE WAS TRAVELING WEST WHICH CAUSED A RUPTURE IN THE DIESEL TANK. IT THEN TRAVELED 4,000 FEET WEST ON THE TRACK, REVERSED DIRECTION AND THEN WENT 2,000 FEET EAST BACK ON THE SAME TRACK. AT THIS TIME THEY NOTICED A RELEASE FROM THE ENGINE, APPLIED A PATCH AND CONTACTED EMERGENCY CREWS. IT WAS DETERMINED THAT ONLY 450 GALLONS OF DIESEL WAS RELEASED. 2 LOCOMOTIVES, AND 0 CARS WERE ON THE TRAIN. INCIDENT DID NOT OCCUR AT A GRADE CROSSING. THE MILEPOST/SUBDIVISION IS STILL UNKNOWN. CLEAN UP IS UNDERWAY. ALL IMPACTED SOIL WILL BE EXCAVATED. THE ORIGINAL REPORTED INFO IS AS FOLLOWS: THE CALLER REPORTED THAT A RAILCAR ON A FREIGHT TRAIN STRUCK A RETARDER, WHICH CREATED A HOLE IN THE CAR. THIS RESULTED IN THE RELEASE OF AN UNKNOWN AMOUNT OF DIESEL FUEL (UP TO 3,000 GALLONS) ONTO BALLAST AND SOIL. NO WATERWAYS OR STORM DRAINS WERE AFFECTED. THE CAUSE OF THE RAILCAR STRIKING THE RETARDER IS UNKNOWN.

properties.summary: Incident Type: MOBILE - NRC Report ID: 939368 - Medium Affected: LAND - Suspected Responsible Party: ADOBE ASPHALT
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 939368
Incident Time: 2010-03-28 16:12:00
Nearest City: Tucson, AZ
Incident Type: MOBILE
Material: ASPHALT
Medium Affected: LAND
Suspected Responsible Party: ADOBE ASPHALT
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 100 gallons
RESPONSIBLE PARTY WAS PULLING A TRAILER THAT HAD LIQUID ASPHALT EMULSION, WHICH IS WATER BASED, GOING TO LOCATIONS TO SEAL DRIVEWAYS. ITEMS IN THE BACK OF THE TRUCK CAUGHT FIRE. THEY DID NOT HAVE A FIRE EXTINGUISHER AVAILABLE TO EXTINGUISH THE FIRE, SO THEY USED THE ASPHALT EMULSION. AFTER AWHILE SOMEONE CALLED 9-1-1 FOR ASSISTANCE. RURAL METRO FIRE DEPARTMENT RESPONDED AND EXTINGUISHED THE FIRE. UPON ARRIVAL, THE OFFICER IN CHARGE NOTICED THE ASPHALT ON THE ROADWAY AND IN THE ROADWAY DRAINAGE DITCH. THE OFFICER REQUESTED ASSISTANCE FROM PIMA COUNTY PUBLIC WORKS AND THE OFFICE OF EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT. THE FIRE DEPT. ESTABLISHED SMALL DAMS TO STOP THE FLOW OF ASPHALT AND WATER FROM THE FIRE EXTINGUISHMENT, TO PREVENT THE LIQUIDS FROM ENTERING THE FINGER WASH. PC PUBLIC WORKS BROUGHT SAND, APPROXIMATELY 7 YARDS, TO COVER THE ASPHALT IN THE STOPPED AREAS. UPON AGREEMENT WITH ALL PARTIES INVOLVED, THE ASPHALT OF THE ROADWAY WAS SPREAD OUT ON THE ROADWAY, TO DRY. PIMA COUNTY PUBLIC WORKS SUPERVISOR AND RESPONSIBLE PARTY AGREED UPON THE CONDITIONS OF THE CLEAN-UP OF THE ASPHALT AND SAND AND ANY DAMAGE TO THE DRAINAGE DITCH.

Report Description///THIS IS A 48HR PHMSA UPDATE FOR NRC REPORT 1340762/// UPDATE:FOLLOWING THE SECOND SUBSEA PIPELINE CUT TO SUPPORT DE-OILING OF THE 12-INCH SOUTH TIMBALIER 130 PIPELINE, PLUMBERS PLUGS WERE INSTALLED ON THE CUT SQUARE ENDS TO MITIGATE FURTHER RELEASE. AFTER THE PLUGS WERE INSTALLED, A FINAL AFTERNOON OVERFLIGHT AT 17:24 CST ON 06JUL22 OBSERVED A BRIGHTLY COLORED SHEEN APPROXIMATELY 800’ X 7,892’ AT THE MAXIMUM POINTS. THE VOLUME WAS ESTIMATED TO BE 30.8 GALLONS, INSTEAD OF THE 13 GALLONS ESTIMATED FROM EARLIER AERIAL SURVEILLANCE AND REPORTED IN NRC #1340762. THE SHEEN WAS NOT SKIMMABLE AND THE ONSITE RESPONSE VESSEL DEPLOYED SORBENT BOOM TO COLLECT THE RECOVERABLE OIL PORTION. AT APPROXIMATELY 21:30 CST ON 06JUL22, DIVERS INSPECTED THE PLUMBER PLUGS AT THE SECOND CUT LOCATION AND NOTED NO DISCHARGE OR LEAKAGE. AT 02:30 CST 07JUL22, THE DIVERS REMOVED THE PLUMBERS PLUG ON THE PIPELINE END OF THE SECOND CUT IN ORDER TO INSTALL THE PERMANENT END CONNECTOR AND PORTED BLIND FLANGE. THE DIVER REPORTED A RELEASE FROM THE PIPELINE DURING THIS OPERATION. A POLLUTION DOME WAS IN PLACE BUT INTERFERED WITH THE RIGGING USED TO SUPPORT THE END CONNECTOR DURING THE CONNECTOR INSTALLATION. THEREFORE, THE POLLUTION DOME WAS UNABLE TO CONTAIN ALL RELEASES. THE SHEEN SIZE OBSERVED FROM THE DIVE BOAT WAS ESTIMATED TO BE 4’ X 30’ WITH AN ESTIMATED RELEASE VOLUME OF 0.125 GALLONS. AERIAL SURVEILLANCE AT 6:20 CST ON 07JUL22 OBSERVED A 50’ X 1,000’ LIGHT SILVERY SHEEN, CONFIRMING THE ESTIMATE OF 0.125 GALLONS. THE TOTAL VOLUME ASSOCIATED WITH SECOND SUBSEA PIPELINE CUT FROM THE START OF THE CUT UNTIL THE PERMANENT END CONNECTOR AND PORTED BLIND FLANGE WERE INSTALLED IS ESTIMATED TO BE 30.925 GALLONS. ORIGINAL: CALLER REPORTED A RELEASE OF 13 GALLONS OF CRUDE OIL FROM A SECOND CUT ON TRANSMISSION PIPELINE AT GIVEN LAT/LONG. RELEASE WAS SECURED TEMPORARILY UNTIL PERMANENT REPAIR CAN BE MADE.
